correctness.rationale: In the barycentric subdivision a chain has at most one face of each cardinality. If two points in the same closed flag simplex are in the same group orbit, the action has to fix every vertex in their support, because its size identifies it uniquely within the closed simplex. The quotient cells thus have embedded closures and are oriented by size, with the signed deletion boundary. I checked the supplied proof and independently constructed the geometric quotient chain complex using injective columns on selected rows and descending flags modulo the stabilizer of the largest face. The run /workspace/branches/check4.py counted 337,3541,10110,11166,4620,360 cells and checked every chain-square identity. Direct integer unit-pivot cancellations, without importing the supplied collapse list/matrix, left ranks (1,0,5,6) with only the degree-three differential nonzero. The entries are all even, and the halved matrix has maximal minors (1,0,0,0,1,0), so the image is exactly twice the entire degree-two chain group. This proves reduced H2=(Z/2)^5, H3=Z, and zero otherwise. The unquotiented comparison is a count of independent torsion summands, not a claim about the image of the induced homology map.
residual_risks: Homology does not classify the homotopy type or fundamental group. Only the ordinary 6-by-6 board and full geometric dihedral quotient are considered.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Enumeration does not specify the integral attaching matrices; standalone descriptions of fixed spaces do not assemble the quotient boundary maps. The inspected published material provides related frameworks, not a stronger quotient-homology theorem covering this case.

evidence: The degree-three character (19,-5,7,-5,1,1,-5,-5) averages to one. Over Q the quotient flag chain complex is the coinvariant complex, and averaging is exact; thus the free ranks are already implied. Averaging is not exact over Z at 2.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior data force the rational rank but not the two-primary elementary divisors of the quotient. In particular, the unquotiented two-torsion and a rational character cannot yield the asserted five order-two summands by a transfer argument.

value.rationale: The six-board queen complex already exhibits an integral torsion class, and the full symmetry quotient of this natural action is a motivated test of torsion under a nonfree quotient. The exact five summands reveal behavior unavailable from the rational character and distinguish the case from the smaller torsion-free quotient. The complete integral groups can be used for comparisons with fixed-space calculations or other coefficient systems without claiming a homotopy classification.
residual_risks: No general law for larger boards or for the image of original torsion classes is established.
